title: Rama doesn't say it twice

verse.sanskrit:
तद्ब्रूहि वचनं देवि राज्ञो यदभिकाङ्क्षितम् ।
करिष्ये प्रतिजाने च रामो द्विर्नाभिभाषते ॥
verse.iast:
tad brūhi vacanaṃ devi rājño yad abhikāṅkṣitam |
kariṣye pratijāne ca rāmo dvir nābhibhāṣate ||
verse.translation: Tell me, queen, what the king wants. I will do it, I promise. Rama does not say things twice.

beats.title: say 'bet' and then ghost
beats.vo: Us: yeah, I'll totally be there. Also us: leaves them on read for three days.
Rama walks into Queen Kaikeyi's room. His father can't even speak. And Kaikeyi says: first promise you'll do whatever the king wants, good or bad. Then I'll tell you what it is.
Anyone else: um, terms and conditions first? Rama is actually hurt she even had to ask. For his father's word, he says, he'd do anything.
Tell me what the king wants. I'll do it, I promise. Rama does not say things twice.
Say it once. Mean it forever. No double texting your own promises.
And what the king wanted was fourteen years in the forest. He kept it anyway. So before your next yes, ask: can I actually keep this? Then say it once.

caption:
Rama would never say 'bet' and then ghost 🫡

Before he even heard what his father wanted, Rama promised to do it. What his father wanted was 14 years in the forest. He kept it anyway.

“तद्ब्रूहि वचनं देवि राज्ञो यदभिकाङ्क्षितम् । करिष्ये प्रतिजाने च रामो द्विर्नाभिभाषते ॥”
Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda 18.30

Say it once. Mean it forever. Day 5 of learning from Rama.
